chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked, 'What does breastfeeding prohibit (from marriage)?' He said, 'That which grows the flesh and strengthens the bone.' I said, 'Does ten feedings prohibit?' He said, 'No, because ten feedings do not grow the flesh nor strengthen the bone.'
ai.seo_question: How many feedings are required for breastfeeding to prohibit marriage in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the criterion for breastfeeding-induced kinship (radāʿ) as the physical maturation of the child, defined by the growth of flesh and strengthening of bone, rather than a fixed number of feedings. He explicitly rejects the notion that ten feedings suffice, arguing that such a small quantity cannot achieve the necessary physiological development to create a permanent mahram relationship. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on functional, biological criteria over rigid numerical counts in deriving legal rulings from the Imams.
